transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-24
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (Clearwave Head of ML), Ethan (Platform), Rita (Security), Samira (SRE), Noah (Product)

Summary (auto): finalizing go-live plan, canary windows, monitoring, smoke tests, rollbacks, and compliance checklist.

00:00 Jordan: okay everyone i think we have a full agenda for today we wanna lock down the rollout plan and make sure the dry-run date works for you all, um quick check-in on blockers?
00:14 Maya: yeah thanks Jordan, no huge blockers on model quality, the eval pass looked good last week, we did see a little spike in tail latency when sequences go > 1k tokens on the test set so we wanna make sure canary covers longer sequences
00:30 Priya: noted, we observed the same in the dedicated runs — kernel selection shifts at that length and it slightly bumps p99. We can include a long-seq canary profile to stress that path.
00:46 Ethan: on infra side, VPC peering is the main item, and also planning for reserved capacity for peak morning windows, but the PO and network approvals are in flight. ETA next week.
01:05 Rita: for security — need to confirm KMS key policy and where audit logs land, SOC 2 doc reqs, and SSO mapping; not blocking cutover but must be validated before production traffic.
01:22 Jordan: great. so propose: dry-run/canary on Dec 8, small percentage traffic (5-10%), 48 hour observation window, then A/B to 25% for 24 hours if metrics look stable, then full cutover. Thoughts?
01:36 Maya: sounds reasonable, but we wanna see specific gating metrics — p95/p99 latency thresholds, error rate threshold, and downstream request error impact.
01:49 Priya: suggested gating: p99 < 800ms for default short prompts, p99 < 1.5s for long sequences, error rate < 0.5% rolling, and no increase in downstream timeouts. Also cost per 1k tokens within agreed band.
02:08 Noah: how do we track the cost gating in real time? we can't have surprises mid-canary.
02:16 Jordan: we'll share a canary dashboard — token burn, estimated cost by model variant, latency histograms, and a live error-rate graph. We can add an alert to Slack and pager on threshold breach.
02:33 Samira: need clear rollback triggers. If p99 spikes by >30% or error rate >0.5% sustained for 10m, we roll back. Also if downstream errors increase more than baseline.
02:46 Priya: agree — we'll automate rollback via feature flagging and policy-based traffic shift back to previous model or to hosted fallback. Redwood supports automatic fallback to smaller model variant in case of high latency or HW OOM.
03:04 Ethan: one nuance — our infra provisioning for dedicated capacity needs a lead time of 72 hours for GPU reservations across the region. If canary hits unexpected throughput then we may need a fast path to burst capacity. Is that supported?
03:18 Jordan: yes, Dedicated supports burst pools; we'll document the burst policy and costs. For pilot we'll use hosted bursts if needed for short window to avoid overcommitting.
03:35 Rita: on compliance — audit logs must retain full request/response metadata for 90 days per our policy. Is that possible with VPC/private deployments?
03:46 Priya: yes, Private deployment supports audit logs to your S3 bucket or SIEM via syslog; we'll provide KMS integration for encryption at rest. We'll share the guide.
03:58 Maya: about smoke tests — what are we running pre-cutover? we need simple functional checks plus throughput ramps and end-to-end product flows.
04:12 Priya: propose smoke suite: 1) auth + SSO check 2) basic generation for short prompts 3) long-seq generation path 4) KV cache hit verification 5) latency regression check 6) end-to-end call that exercises downstream worker.
04:30 Jordan: and we should run canary with synthetic traffic shaped to match production token distribution — not just uniform requests. Priya will share the traffic profile.
04:44 Maya: can we get the runbook template now or is it later?
04:49 Jordan: we'll send runbook draft today or tomorrow, include step-by-step cutover, rollback, stakeholders, contacts, run commands, dashboards, and checklists.
04:59 Noah: one open question is data residency — some customers require tokens not to leave region, do we need to validate where host runs?
05:08 Priya: can pin region; Redwood can route to region-specific pools and we can ensure model variants are in the customer's private deployment or dedicated region. We'll include region mapping in the runbook.
05:20 Rita: two security things: 1) define who can trigger a rollback (roles), 2) ensure we have two-person approval for production cutover.
05:30 Jordan: noted, we'll add RBAC steps and approval gates to runbook.
05:36 Samira: for monitoring, we need SLOs and runbook actions mapped to pager alerts; i.e. if canary latency crosses threshold, first action is pause traffic, then run diagnostic script. Make that automated where possible.
05:53 Priya: Redwood's tracing hooks can export span traces; we'll provide a sample tracing view to correlate model latency to downstream service times.
06:05 Maya: what about A/B test vs canary? are we doing both?
06:11 Jordan: plan is canary first to validate infra/ops with small percent. A/B (routing different model variants to different user cohorts) is optional but we can schedule a short A/B for quality comparisons after canary. It requires product flags on your side.
06:28 Noah: product team prefers canary then a limited A/B to confirm UX metrics. ok.
06:34 Priya: small note — in earlier dedicated runs we saw cache cold-starts add ~200ms for first request; include warmup steps in runbook (pre-warm KV cache).
06:47 Jordan: we'll include warmup scripts. Also, we'll send sample smoke test harness and a link to the benchmark spreadsheet we used.
06:55 Ethan: re: cost — can we set an automated stop if spend per hour > X?
07:02 Jordan: yes we can put cost alerts; we'll add a budget guard in the dashboard. Not ideal to auto-cut in middle of canary but we can pause traffic if spending exceeds agreed band.
07:16 Rita: last compliance Q: logging PII — can we strip sensitive fields before persisting logs?
07:24 Priya: yes, Redwood supports field-level redaction and we can show configuration. We'll include that in KMS/audit doc.
07:36 Jordan: wrapping up — agreed actions and dry-run date Dec 8. Any other comments?
07:42 Maya: thanks all, looks good. We'll confirm VPC peering ETA by end of week.
07:47 Jordan: perfect. we'll send runbook and dashboard by Thursday. thanks everyone.

Recap: Dry-run 2026-12-08; 5-10% traffic then progressive ramp if metrics OK; runbook + canary dashboard to be shared; VPC peering and KMS validation tasks for Clearwave; smoke tests and rollback automation defined.

References/Links: canary-dashboard (link to be shared), runbook-template (link to be shared), benchmark spreadsheet (link to be shared).

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had a few name mismatches and punctuation gaps. Some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (KV cache -> K V cache, kernel selection -> kenal selection).
